english.title: Person without jurisdiction administering oath - Statutory Declaration Act 1835

english.legislation: Contrary to section 13 of the Statutory Declaration Act 1835 and section 32 of the Magistrates Courts Act 1980.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
administered/caused to allow to be administered/received/ caused or allowed to be received
an oath/affidavit/a solemn affirmation touching any matter or thing whereof
he/she did not have jurisdiction or cognisance by some statute

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: This offence should not be construed to extend to any oath, affidavit, or solemn affirmation before any justice in any matter or thing touching the preservation of the peace, or the prosecution, trial, or punishment of offences, or touching any proceedings before either of the Houses of Parliament or any committee thereof respectively, nor to any oath, affidavit, or affirmation which may be required by the laws of any foreign country to give validity to instruments in writing designed to be used in such foreign countries respectively.

other.penalty:
Summary: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine of the proscribed sum.
Indictment: Imprisonment and / or a fine

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
